ধন-দণ্ড লয়, আর করায় মিনতি ॥ ২১০ ॥

lakṣmīra caraṇe āni’ karāya praṇati
to Lakṣmī’s feet bringing they make bow
dhana-daṇḍa laya, āra karāya minati
a fine in money they take and they make plead

210At Lakṣmī’s feet they made them bow down; they exacted a fine from them and made them plead humbly.

রথের উপরে করে দণ্ডের তাড়ন ৷
চোর-প্রায় করে জগন্নাথের সেবকগণ ॥ ২১১ ॥

rathera upare kare daṇḍera tāḍana
the chariot upon they do with sticks beating
cora-prāya kare jagannāthera sevaka-gaṇa
almost like thieves they treat Jagannātha’s servants

211They beat the chariot with sticks and treated Jagannātha’s servants almost like thieves.

সব ভৃত্যগণ কহে, — যোড় করি’ হাত ৷
কালি আনি দিব তোমার আগে জগন্নাথ ॥ ২১২ ॥

saba bhṛtya-gaṇa kahe, — yoḍa kari’ hāta
all the servants say joined making hands
kāli āni diba tomāra āge jagannātha
tomorrow bringing we shall give your before Jagannātha

212All the servants said with folded hands, ‘Tomorrow we shall bring Jagannātha before you.’

তবে শান্ত হঞা লক্ষ্মী যায় নিজ ঘর ৷
আমার লক্ষ্মীর সম্পদ্ — বাক্য-অগোচর ॥ ২১৩ ॥

tabe śānta hañā lakṣmī yāya nija ghara
then pacified becoming Lakṣmī goes to her own home
āmāra lakṣmīra sampad — vākya-agocara
of my Lakṣmī the wealth beyond words

213Then Lakṣmī, pacified, went back to her own home. The wealth of my Lakṣmī is beyond words!

দুগ্ধ আউটি’ দধি মথে তোমার গোপীগণে ৷
আমার ঠাকুরাণী বৈসে রত্নসিংহাসনে ॥ ২১৪ ॥

dugdha āuṭi’ dadhi mathe tomāra gopī-gaṇe
milk boiling yogurt churn your gopīs
āmāra ṭhākurāṇī vaise ratna-siṁhāsane
my mistress sits on a jeweled throne

214Your gopīs boil milk and churn yogurt, while my mistress sits on a jewelled throne.”45

নারদ-প্রকৃতি শ্রীবাস করে পরিহাস ৷
শুনি’ হাসে মহাপ্রভুর যত নিজ-দাস ॥ ২১৫ ॥

nārada-prakṛti śrīvāsa kare parihāsa
of Nārada’s nature Śrīvāsa makes jokes
śuni’ hāse mahāprabhura yata nija-dāsa
hearing laugh Mahāprabhu’s all own servants

215Śrīvāsa, whose nature is like Nārada’s, joked in this way, and all of Mahāprabhu’s own servants laughed to hear him.46

প্রভু কহে, — শ্রীবাস, তোমাতে নারদ-স্বভাব ৷
ঐশ্বর্যভাবে তোমাতে, ঈশ্বর-প্রভাব ॥ ২১৬ ॥

prabhu kahe, — śrīvāsa, tomāte nārada-svabhāva
the Lord says Śrīvāsa in you Nārada’s nature
aiśvarya-bhāve tomāte, īśvara-prabhāva
in the mood of majesty on you the Lord’s influence

216The Lord said, “Śrīvāsa, you have Nārada’s nature: in the mood of majesty (aiśvarya), the Lord’s power holds sway over you.

ইঁহো দামোদর-স্বরূপ — শুদ্ধ-ব্রজবাসী ৷
ঐশ্বর্য্য না জানে ইঁহো শুদ্ধপ্রেমে ভাসি’ ॥ ২১৭ ॥

im̐ho dāmodara-svarūpa — śuddha-vrajavāsī
he Dāmodara Svarūpa a pure resident of Vraja
aiśvarya nā jāne im̐ho śuddha-preme bhāsi’
majesty not knows he in pure love floating

217But this Svarūpa Dāmodara is a pure resident of Vraja. Floating in pure love, he does not know majesty.”

স্বরূপ কহে, — শ্রীবাস, শুন সাবধানে ৷
বৃন্দাবনসম্পদ্ তোমার নাহি পড়ে মনে ? ॥ ২১৮ ॥

svarūpa kahe, — śrīvāsa, śuna sāvadhāne
Svarūpa says Śrīvāsa listen attentively
vṛndāvana-sampad tomāra nāhi paḍe mane?
the wealth of Vṛndāvana your not comes to mind

218Svarūpa said, “Śrīvāsa, listen carefully! Does the wealth of Vṛndāvana not come to your mind?

বৃন্দাবনে সাহজিক যে সম্পৎসিন্ধু ৷
দ্বারকা-বৈকুণ্ঠ-সম্পৎ — তার এক বিন্দু ॥ ২১৯ ॥

vṛndāvane sāhajika ye sampat-sindhu
in Vṛndāvana natural which ocean of wealth
dvārakā-vaikuṇṭha-sampat-tāra eka bindu
of Dvārakā and Vaikuṇṭha the wealth of it one drop

219In Vṛndāvana there is a natural ocean of wealth, and the wealth of Dvārakā and Vaikuṇṭha is but a drop of it.

পরম পুরুষোত্তম স্বয়ং ভগবান্ ৷
কৃষ্ণ যাঁহা ধনী তাঁহা বৃন্দাবন-ধাম ॥ ২২০ ॥

parama puruṣottama svayaṁ bhagavān
the supreme Puruṣottama Himself Bhagavān
kṛṣṇa yām̐hā dhanī tām̐hā vṛndāvana-dhāma
Kṛṣṇa where the owner of wealth there the abode of Vṛndāvana

220Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Puruṣottama, Bhagavān Himself, and where He is rich, there is His abode, Vṛndāvana.47

চিন্তামণিময় ভূমি, রত্নের ভবন ৷
চিন্তামণিগণ — দাসী-চরণ-ভূষণ ॥ ২২১ ॥

cintāmaṇi-maya bhūmi, ratnera bhavana
made of cintāmaṇi the ground of jewels the houses
cintāmaṇi-gaṇa — dāsī-caraṇa-bhūṣaṇa
cintāmaṇi gems of the maidservants the foot ornaments

221There the ground is made of cintāmaṇi gems and the houses of jewels; cintāmaṇi gems are the ornaments on the maidservants’ feet.

কল্পবৃক্ষ-লতার — যাঁহা সাহজিক-বন ৷
পুষ্প-ফল বিনা কেহ না মাগে অন্য ধন ॥ ২২২ ॥

kalpavṛkṣa-latāra — yām̐hā sāhajika-vana
of wish-fulfilling trees and creepers where a natural forest
puṣpa-phala vinā keha nā māge anya dhana
flowers and fruits except no one not asks for other wealth

222There the natural forest is made of wish-fulfilling trees and creepers, yet no one asks them for any wealth but flowers and fruits.

অনন্ত কামধেনু তাঁহা ফিরে বনে বনে ৷
দুগ্ধমাত্র দেন, কেহ না মাগে অন্য ধনে ॥ ২২৩ ॥

ananta kāma-dhenu tām̐hā phire vane vane
countless wish-fulfilling cows there wander from forest to forest
dugdha-mātra dena, keha nā māge anya dhane
milk only they give no one not asks for other wealth

223Countless wish-fulfilling cows wander there from forest to forest; they give only milk, and no one asks them for any other wealth.

সহজ লোকের কথা — যাঁহা দিব্য-গীত ৷
সহজ গমন করে, — যৈছে নৃত্য-প্রতীত ॥ ২২৪ ॥

sahaja lokera kathā — yām̐hā divya-gīta
ordinary of the people the talk where a divine song
sahaja gamana kare, — yaiche nṛtya-pratīta
ordinary walking they do as is taken for dancing

224There the ordinary talk of the people is a divine song, and their ordinary walking seems like dancing.

সর্ব্বত্র জল — যাঁহা অমৃত-সমান ৷
চিদানন্দ জ্যোতিঃ স্বাদ্য — যাঁহা মূর্ত্তিমান্ ॥ ২২৫ ॥

sarvatra jala — yām̐hā amṛta-samāna
everywhere the water where like nectar
cid-ānanda jyotiḥ svādya — yām̐hā mūrtimān
spiritual and blissful the light to be relished where embodied

225Everywhere the water is like nectar, and the light of spiritual bliss takes form there, to be relished.48

লক্ষ্মী জিনি’ গুণ যাঁহা লক্ষ্মীর সমাজ ৷
কৃষ্ণ-বংশী করে যাঁহা প্রিয়সখী-কায ॥ ২২৬ ॥

lakṣmī jini’ guṇa yām̐hā lakṣmīra samāja
Lakṣmī surpassing in qualities where of Lakṣmīs the company
kṛṣṇa-vaṁśī kare yām̐hā priya-sakhī-kāya
Kṛṣṇa’s flute does where of a dear friend the service

226There the gopīs, a whole society of Lakṣmīs, surpass Lakṣmī in their qualities, and Kṛṣṇa’s flute serves as a dear friend.49

শ্রিয়ঃ কান্তাঃ কান্তঃ পরমপুরুষঃ কল্পতরবো
দ্রুমা ভূমিশ্চিন্তামণিগণময়ী তোয়মমৃতম্ ৷
কথা গানং নাট্যং গমনমপি বংশী প্রিয়সখী ৷
চিদানন্দং জ্যোতিঃ পরমপি তদাস্বাদ্যমপি চ ॥ ২২৭ ॥

śriyaḥ kāntāḥ kāntaḥ parama-puruṣaḥ kalpa-taravo
goddesses of fortune the beloveds the lover the Supreme Person wish-fulfilling trees
drumā bhūmiś cintāmaṇi-gaṇa-mayī toyam amṛtam
the trees the ground made of cintāmaṇi gems the water nectar
kathā gānaṁ nāṭyaṁ gamanam api vaṁśī priya-sakhī
speech song dance walking also the flute a dear friend
cid-ānandaṁ jyotiḥ param api tad āsvādyam api ca
spiritual and blissful light the supreme also that to be relished also and

227“There the beloveds are goddesses of fortune and the lover is the Supreme Person; the trees are wish-fulfilling trees; the ground is made of cintāmaṇi gems and the water is nectar; speech is song and walking is dance; the flute is a dear friend; and the supreme light is spiritual bliss, there to be relished.” (Brahma-saṁhitā, 5.56)50

চিন্তামণিশ্চরণভূষণমঙ্গনানাং
শৃঙ্গারপুষ্পতরবস্তরবঃ সুরাণাম্ ৷
বৃন্দাবনে ব্রজধনং ননু কামধেনু-
বৃন্দানি চেতি সুখসিন্ধুরহো বিভূতিঃ ॥ ২২৮ ॥

cintāmaṇiś caraṇa-bhūṣaṇam aṅganānāṁ
cintāmaṇi the foot ornament of the maidens
śṛṅgāra-puṣpa-taravas taravaḥ surāṇām
trees with flowers for adornment the trees of the gods
vṛndāvane vraja-dhanaṁ nanu kāma-dhenu-
in Vṛndāvana the wealth of Vraja indeed of wish-fulfilling cows
vṛndāni ceti sukha-sindhur aho vibhūtiḥ
herds and thus an ocean of happiness ah! the splendour

228“In Vṛndāvana cintāmaṇi is the ornament of the maidens’ feet; the trees of the gods supply the flowers for their adornment; and the wealth of Vraja is herds of wish-fulfilling cows. Ah, this splendour is an ocean of happiness!” (Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, 2.1.173)51

শুনি’ প্রেমাবেশে নৃত্য করে শ্রীনিবাস ৷
কক্ষতালি বাজায়, করে অট্ট-অট্ট হাস ॥ ২২৯ ॥

śuni’ premāveśe nṛtya kare śrīnivāsa
hearing in the rapture of love dance does Śrīnivāsa
kakṣa-tāli bājāya, kare aṭṭa-aṭṭa hāsa
under the arm clapping he sounds he makes loud loud laughter

229Hearing this, Śrīvāsa danced in the rapture of love, clapping his hands under his arms and laughing loudly.

রাধার শুদ্ধরস প্রভু আবেশে শুনিল ৷
সেই রসাবেশে প্রভু নৃত্য আরম্ভিল ॥ ২৩০ ॥

rādhāra śuddha-rasa prabhu āveśe śunila
Rādhā’s pure rasa the Lord in rapture heard
sei rasāveśe prabhu nṛtya ārambhila
in that rapture of rasa the Lord dance began

230In rapture the Lord heard of Rādhā’s pure rasa, and, overwhelmed by that rasa, He began to dance.

রসাবেশে প্রভুর নৃত্য, স্বরূপের গান ৷
‘বল’ ‘বল’ বলি’ প্রভু পাতে নিজ-কাণ ॥ ২৩১ ॥

rasāveśe prabhura nṛtya, svarūpera gāna
in the rapture of rasa the Lord’s dance Svarūpa’s singing
‘bala’ ‘bala’ bali’ prabhu pāte nija-kāṇa
go on go on saying the Lord lends His own ears

231Absorbed in rasa, the Lord danced and Svarūpa sang. “Sing on, sing on!” the Lord kept saying, all ears.

ব্রজরস-গীত শুনি’ প্রেম উথলিল ৷
পুরুষোত্তম-গ্রাম প্রভু প্রেমে ভাসাইল ॥ ২৩২ ॥

vraja-rasa-gīta śuni’ prema uthalila
songs of the rasa of Vraja hearing love surged up
puruṣottama-grāma prabhu preme bhāsāila
the town of Puruṣottama the Lord with love flooded

232As He heard the songs of Vraja’s rasa, His love welled up, and the Lord flooded the town of Puruṣottama with it.

লক্ষ্মী-দেবী-যথাকালে গেলা নিজ-ঘর ৷
প্রভু নৃত্য করে, হৈল দ্বিতীয় প্রহর ॥ ২৩৩ ॥

lakṣmī-devī-yathā-kāle gelā nija-ghara
Lakṣmī-devī in due time went to her own home
prabhu nṛtya kare, haila dvitīya prahara
the Lord dance does came the second watch

233In due time Lakṣmī-devī went back to her own home. The Lord went on dancing, and the second watch of the day (prahara) had come.

চারি সম্প্রদায় গান করি’ বহু শ্রান্ত হৈল ৷
মহাপ্রভুর প্রেমাবেশে দ্বিগুণ বাড়িল ॥ ২৩৪ ॥

cāri sampradāya gāna kari’ bahu śrānta haila
the four groups singing having done very tired became
mahāprabhura premāveśe dviguṇa bāḍila
Mahāprabhu’s in the rapture of love twofold increased

234The four groups grew very tired from singing, but Mahāprabhu’s rapture of love doubled.

রাধা-প্রেমাবেশে প্রভু হৈলা সেই মূর্ত্তি ৷
নিত্যানন্দ দূরে দেখি’ করিলেন স্তুতি ॥ ২৩৫ ॥

rādhā-premāveśe prabhu hailā sei mūrti
in the rapture of Rādhā’s love the Lord became that form
nityānanda dūre dekhi’ karilena stuti
Nityānanda from afar seeing offered prayers

235In the rapture of Rādhā’s love the Lord assumed Her very form. Seeing this from afar, Nityānanda offered prayers.

নিত্যানন্দ দেখিয়া প্রভুর ভাবাবেশ ৷
নিকটে না আইসে, কিছু রহে দূরদেশ ॥ ২৩৬ ॥

nityānanda dekhiyā prabhura bhāvāveśa
Nityānanda seeing the Lord’s rapture of feeling
nikaṭe nā āise, kichu rahe dūra-deśa
near not comes somewhat stays at a distance

236Seeing the Lord’s rapture, Nityānanda would not come near but kept somewhat at a distance.52

নিত্যানন্দ বিনা প্রভুকে ধরে কোন্ জন ৷
প্রভুর আবেশ না যায়, না রহে কীর্ত্তন ॥ ২৩৭ ॥

nityānanda vinā prabhuke dhare kon jana
Nityānanda except the Lord holds what person
prabhura āveśa nā yāya, nā rahe kīrtana
the Lord’s rapture not goes not stops the kīrtana

237Who but Nityānanda could hold the Lord? His rapture did not subside, and the kīrtana did not stop.

ভঙ্গি করি’ স্বরূপ সবার শ্রম জানাইল ৷
ভক্তগণের শ্রম দেখি’ প্রভুর বাহ্য হৈল ॥ ২৩৮ ॥

bhaṅgi kari’ svarūpa sabāra śrama jānāila
a stratagem making Svarūpa of all the fatigue made known
bhakta-gaṇera śrama dekhi’ prabhura bāhya haila
of the devotees the fatigue seeing the Lord’s outer awareness came

238By a skilful hint Svarūpa made the Lord aware of everyone’s fatigue, and seeing how tired the devotees were, the Lord returned to outer awareness.

সব ভক্ত লঞা প্রভু গেলা পুষ্পোদ্যানে ৷
বিশ্রাম করিয়া কৈলা মাধ্যাহ্নিক-স্নানে ॥ ২৩৯ ॥

saba bhakta lañā prabhu gelā puṣpodyāne
all devotees taking the Lord went to the flower garden
viśrāma kariyā kailā mādhyāhnika-snāne
rest having taken He did the midday bath

239Taking all the devotees with Him, the Lord went to the flower garden; there He rested and then took His midday bath.

জগন্নাথের প্রসাদ আইল বহু উপহার ৷
লক্ষ্মীর প্রসাদ আইল বিবিধ প্রকার ॥ ২৪০ ॥

jagannāthera prasāda āila bahu upahāra
Jagannātha’s prasāda came many offerings
lakṣmīra prasāda āila vividha prakāra
Lakṣmī’s prasāda came various kinds

240Many offerings of Jagannātha’s prasāda arrived, and with them Lakṣmī’s prasāda of every kind.53

সবা লঞা নানা-রঙ্গে করিলা ভোজন ৷
সন্ধ্যা স্নান করি’ কৈল জগন্নাথ দরশন ॥ ২৪১ ॥

sabā lañā nānā-raṅge karilā bhojana
all taking with many delights He did eating
sandhyā snāna kari’ kaila jagannātha daraśana
evening bath having taken He did Jagannātha’s darśana

241With everyone around Him, the Lord ate joyfully. After His evening bath He went for darśana of Jagannātha.

জগন্নাথ দেখি’ করেন নর্ত্তন-কীর্ত্তন ৷
নরেন্দ্রে জলক্রীড়া করে লঞা ভক্তগণ ॥ ২৪২ ॥

jagannātha dekhi’ karena nartana-kīrtana
Jagannātha seeing He does dancing and kīrtana
narendre jala-krīḍā kare lañā bhakta-gaṇa
in Narendra water sports He does taking the devotees

242Seeing Jagannātha, He danced and sang kīrtana; then He played in the water of Narendra Lake with the devotees.

উদ্যানে আসিয়া কৈল বন-ভোজন ৷
এইমত ক্রীড়া কৈল প্রভু অষ্ট দিন ॥ ২৪৩ ॥

udyāne āsiyā kaila vana-bhojana
to the garden coming He did a forest meal
ei-mata krīḍā kaila prabhu aṣṭa dina
in this way pastimes did the Lord eight days

243Coming to the garden, He had a meal in the grove. In this way the Lord enjoyed His pastimes for eight days.

আর দিনে জগন্নাথের ভিতর-বিজয় ৷
রথে চড়ি’ জগন্নাথ চলে নিজালয় ॥ ২৪৪ ॥

āra dine jagannāthera bhitara-vijaya
on the next day Jagannātha’s return within
rathe caḍi’ jagannātha cale nijālaya
on the chariot mounting Jagannātha goes to His own abode

244The next day was Jagannātha’s return (bhitara-vijaya): mounting His chariot, He went back to His own abode.

পূর্ব্ববৎ কৈল প্রভু লঞা ভক্তগণ ৷
পরম আনন্দে করেন নর্ত্তন-কীর্ত্তন ॥ ২৪৫ ॥

pūrvavat kaila prabhu lañā bhakta-gaṇa
as before did the Lord with the devotees
parama ānande karena nartana-kīrtana
in supreme bliss He does dancing and kīrtana

245As before, the Lord, together with the devotees, danced and sang kīrtana in supreme bliss.

জগন্নাথের পুনঃ পাণ্ডু-বিজয় হইল ৷
এক-গুটি পট্টডোরী তাঁহা টুটি’ গেল ॥ ২৪৬ ॥

jagannāthera punaḥ pāṇḍu-vijaya haila
Jagannātha’s again pāṇḍu-vijaya took place
eka-guṭi paṭṭa-ḍorī tām̐hā ṭuṭi’ gela
one silk rope there breaking went

246Once again Jagannātha’s pāṇḍu-vijaya took place, and one of the silk ropes broke.54

পাণ্ডু-বিজয়ের তুলী ফাটি-ফুটি যায় ৷
জগন্নাথের ভরে তুলা উড়িয়া পলায় ॥ ২৪৭ ॥

pāṇḍu-vijayera tulī phāṭi-phuṭi yāya
of the pāṇḍu-vijaya the cotton pads tearing and bursting go
jagannāthera bhare tulā uḍiyā palāya
of Jagannātha by the weight the cotton flying up scatters

247The cotton pads used for the pāṇḍu-vijaya tore and burst, and under Jagannātha’s weight the cotton flew up and scattered.

কুলীনগ্রামী রামানন্দ, সত্যরাজ খাঁন ৷
তাঁরে আজ্ঞা দিল প্রভু করিয়া সম্মান ॥ ২৪৮ ॥

kulīna-grāmī rāmānanda, satyarāja khām̐na
of Kulīna-grāma Rāmānanda Satyarāja Khān
tām̐re ājñā dila prabhu kariyā sammāna
to them an order gave the Lord showing respect

248Rāmānanda and Satyarāja Khān of Kulīna-grāma were there, and the Lord respectfully gave them an order:

এই পট্টডোরীর তুমি হও যজমান ৷
প্রতিবৎসর আনিবে ‘ডোরী’ করিয়া নির্ম্মাণ ॥ ২৪৯ ॥

ei paṭṭa-ḍorīra tumi hao yajamāna
of these silk ropes you be the patrons
prati-vatsara ānibe ‘ḍorī’ kariyā nirmāṇa
every year bring ropes having made

249“Be the patrons (yajamāna) of these silk ropes: every year have the ropes made and bring them here.”55

এত বলি’ দিল তাঁরে ছিণ্ডা পট্টডোরী ৷
ইহা দেখি’ করিবে ডোরী অতি দৃঢ় করি’ ॥ ২৫০ ॥

eta bali’ dila tām̐re chiṇḍā paṭṭa-ḍorī
so saying gave to them the torn silk rope
ihā dekhi’ karibe ḍorī ati dṛḍha kari’
this seeing make ropes very strong making

250So saying, He gave them the torn silk rope. “Look at this,” He said, “and make the ropes very strong.

এই পট্টডোরীতে হয় ‘শেষ’-অধিষ্ঠান ৷
দশ-মূর্ত্তি হঞা যেঁহো সেবে ভগবান্ ॥ ২৫১ ॥

ei paṭṭa-ḍorīte haya ‘śeṣa’-adhiṣṭhāna
in this silk rope is Śeṣa’s abode
daśa-mūrti hañā yem̐ho seve bhagavān
in ten forms becoming who serves Bhagavān

251In this silk rope resides Śeṣa, who serves Bhagavān by assuming ten forms.”

ভাগ্যবান্ সেই সত্যরাজ, রামানন্দ ৷
সেবা আজ্ঞা পাঞা হৈল পরম আনন্দ ॥ ২৫২ ॥

bhāgyavān sei satyarāja, rāmānanda
fortunate those Satyarāja Rāmānanda
sevā ājñā pāñā haila parama ānanda
of service the order receiving became supreme bliss

252Fortunate indeed were Satyarāja and Rāmānanda: receiving the order to serve, they felt supreme bliss.

প্রতি বৎসর গুণ্ডিচাতে ভক্তগণ-সঙ্গে ৷
পট্টডোরী লঞা আইসে অতি বড় রঙ্গে ॥ ২৫৩ ॥

prati vatsara guṇḍicāte bhakta-gaṇa-saṅge
every year to the Guṇḍicā with the devotees
paṭṭa-ḍorī lañā āise ati baḍa raṅge
silk ropes bringing they come with very great joy

253Every year after that, they came with the devotees to the Guṇḍicā festival with great joy, bringing silk ropes.

তবে জগন্নাথ যাই’ বসিলা সিংহাসনে ৷
মহাপ্রভু ঘরে আইলা লঞা ভক্তগণে ॥ ২৫৪ ॥

tabe jagannātha yāi’ vasilā siṁhāsane
then Jagannātha going sat on His throne
mahāprabhu ghare āilā lañā bhakta-gaṇe
Mahāprabhu home came with the devotees

254Then Jagannātha went and sat upon His throne, and Mahāprabhu came home with the devotees.

এইমত ভক্তগণে যাত্রা দেখাইল ৷
ভক্তগণ লঞা বৃন্দাবন-কেলি কৈল ॥ ২৫৫ ॥

ei-mata bhakta-gaṇe yātrā dekhāila
in this way to the devotees the festival He showed
bhakta-gaṇa lañā vṛndāvana-keli kaila
the devotees with the pastimes of Vṛndāvana He enacted

255In this way the Lord showed the devotees the Herā-pañcamī festival and, together with them, enacted the pastimes of Vṛndāvana.56

চৈতন্য-গোসাঞির লীলা — অনন্ত, অপার ৷
‘সহস্র-বদন’ যার নাহি পায় পার ॥ ২৫৬ ॥

caitanya-gosāñira līlā — ananta, apāra
of Caitanya Gosāñi the pastimes endless boundless
‘sahasra-vadana’ yāra nāhi pāya pāra
the thousand-mouthed one of which not reaches the end

256The pastimes of Caitanya Gosāñi are endless and boundless; even the thousand-mouthed Śeṣa cannot reach their end.

শ্রীরূপ-রঘুনাথ-পদে যার আশ ৷
চৈতন্যচরিতামৃত কহে কৃষ্ণদাস ॥ ২৫৭ ॥

śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
Śrī Rūpa’s, Raghunātha’s at the feet whose hope
caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
“Caitanya-caritāmṛta” narrates Kṛṣṇadāsa

257Praying at the feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate the Caitanya-caritāmṛta.57

✦

Notes

  1. Heading in the edition: “Gaurasundara dances as He watches the Herā-pañcamī.” Anubhāṣya: gopī-rasollāsa is the highest pitch of the gopīs’ parakīya-rasa.
  2. The second line is the same as Ādi 12.2; translation as there.
  3. The first line is the same as Ādi 9.3 and Madhya 12.3; translation as there.
  4. Heading in the edition: “Dressed as a humble Vaiṣṇava, with the permission of all the Vaiṣṇavas, [the king] massages the feet of the Lord, who lies with His eyes closed.”
  5. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: the chapter “Jayati te ’dhikam” is the Gopī-gītā, one of the five chapters of the rāsa dance (Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 10.31). Heading in the edition: “The king recites the Gopī-gītā.”
  6. Anubhāṣya: the gopīs sing this verse when Kṛṣṇa has vanished from the rāsa dance; tapta-jīvanam — the life of those who burn in separation from Him; kalmaṣāpaham — taking away the anguish of the fever of separation; kavi — those who know the rasa of Kṛṣṇa. Heading in the edition: “One who gives away the nectar of the Lord’s narrations is the most munificent of givers.”
  7. Heading in the edition: “Unaware [of who was before Him, the Lord] embraces the king.” Anubhāṣya: the first iṅho is Mahāprabhu, the second the king Pratāparudra.
  8. Heading in the edition: “Caitanya’s mercy does not weigh a person’s fitness and needs no cause.”
  9. Heading in the edition: “The king introduces himself as ‘a servant of the servants of Kṛṣṇa’.”
  10. Heading in the edition: “The all-knowing Lord, in His outer consciousness, does not reveal that in the trance of love He had seen the king.”
  11. Heading in the edition: “After the midday bath Vāṇīnātha brings abundant prasāda for all.”
  12. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: ni-sakaḍi is yogurt, thickened milk (kṣīra), fruits, roots and everything else that is not sakaḍi, food cooked in water. Anubhāṣya: the list in verses 25–34 shows how well the author knows the whole variety of offerings to Kṛṣṇa.
  13. Anubhāṣya: bīja-tāla is the soft kernel of the palm fruit (tāla-śāṁs).
  14. Anubhāṣya: saravatī is a choice kind of lemon; another reading of amṛta-maṇḍā is amṛta-bhāṇḍa, papaya.
  15. Anubhāṣya: ḍāli-marica-lāḍu are balls made of mung; navāta is a sweet boiled in sugar syrup; amṛti is a sweet fried in ghee, like jilipi.
  16. Anubhāṣya: candrakānti are thin flatbreads of urad dal or puffed moon-shaped baḍis; viyari is a flatbread of puffed rice; kadmā is a very hard sweet of rice flour in sugar syrup; tilā-khājā is khājā with sesame fried in ghee.
  17. Heading in the edition: “Gaurahari watches the beggars eat and teaches them to sing the name of Hari.”
  18. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: the nine days of the festival at Guṇḍicā’s house are called the nava-rātra-yātrā; all those days the Lord stayed with the devotees at Āiṭoṭā, and the nine chief devotees headed by Advaita invited Him, each on his own day.
  19. Heading in the edition: “The joy of the Lord, who is in the mood of a gopī, a maidservant of Śrī Rādhā, that Kṛṣṇa has come to Vraja and met Śrī Rādhā.”
  20. Anubhāṣya: gaṇḍa-śaila — small hills; though “these two” are named, the words are aimed above all at Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya.
  21. Anubhāṣya: before he received Mahāprabhu’s mercy, Sārvabhauma knew only the impersonal Brahman and followed the path of logic, so Gopīnātha likened him to the oil-presser’s ox that eats the oilcake.
  22. Anubhāṣya: although the Lord began the pastimes of Vṛndāvana here, He has no pastimes as the enjoyer (bhoktā) such as Kṛṣṇa has in parakīya-rasa: He thinks of Himself as a maidservant of Śrī Rādhā and is immersed in an ocean of bliss when Rādhā meets Kṛṣṇa, and it was in this mood that He enjoyed the vṛndāvana-vihāra with the devotees (cf. verses 73–75). The teaching of gaura-nāgarī therefore has no place here at all.
  23. Heading in the edition: “The Lord rests at Jagannātha-vallabha.” Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: the garden Jagannātha-vallabha lies about halfway between Guṇḍicā-bāḍī and the temple; there the pastime of “stealing the danā” takes place: Śrī Madana-mohana comes there and carries off the fragrant plant called danā.
  24. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: the Herā-pañcamī is the fifth day after the Ratha-yātrā: Lakṣmī-devī, searching for Jagannātha, goes to Guṇḍicā, and having seen (heriyā) Him she returns; this is why the people of Utkala call the day “Herā-pañcamī”.
  25. Heading in the edition: “He arranges for the Lord to watch at His ease.”
  26. Heading in the edition: “Kāśī Miśra seats the Lord in the best place.”
  27. Anubhāṣya: out of compassion for the jīvas, Śrī Jagannāthadeva sits in the temple at Nīlācala and shows Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes of Dvārakā; once a year there awakens in Him an intense longing to see Sundarācala, which is like Vṛndāvana.
  28. Anubhāṣya: Lakṣmī cannot take part in the pastimes of Vṛndāvana, and so Jagannātha does not take her with Him when He goes to Sundarācala.
  29. Anubhāṣya: see Bṛhad-bhāgavatāmṛta, part 1, chapter 7.
  30. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: as He sets out, Jagannātha tells Lakṣmī, “I shall be back tomorrow,” but two or three days pass, and Lakṣmī in her love, seeing even a shadow of indifference in her Beloved, by her very nature flares up in anger. Heading in the edition: “Svarūpa gives the reason: when the beloved is indifferent, the loving woman becomes angry and offended.”
  31. Heading in the edition: “Lakṣmī comes in great pomp with many maidservants.”
  32. Heading in the edition: “Such too is the māna of the gopīs of Vraja and of Satyabhāmā.” Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: such is the māna of the gopīs in Vraja, and Satyabhāmā shows the same, but Lakṣmī’s māna is the very opposite.
  33. Anubhāṣya: on the kinds of heroines, of group leaders and of friends, see the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi.
  34. Anubhāṣya: rasābhāsa is a “semblance of rasa”, a rasa in which its defining marks are distorted (Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, Uttara-vibhāga, 9th wave); it is of three kinds — uparasa, anurasa and aparasa.
  35. Anubhāṣya: avaruddha-saurata — He is ātmārāma, the transcendental Kāmadeva. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: the gopīs, Vṛndāvana, those nights and the rāsa dance itself are wholly spiritual; Kṛṣṇa never so much as glances at material love.
  36. Anubhāṣya (after the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi): the vāmā heroine is ever ready for māna, is angered when it slackens and does not yield to the hero; the dakṣiṇā cannot bear prolonged māna and softens at his tender words.
  37. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: in age She is madhyā, by nature samā, and always vāmā; from this contrariness māna is born.
  38. The same verse as Madhya 8.110; translation as there.
  39. Anubhāṣya (after the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi): when the sāttvika-anubhāvas of rūḍha-bhāva reach an indescribable distinction, this is called adhirūḍha-mahābhāva.
  40. Bibboka — so spelt in the edition and the commentaries (বিব্বোক). Anubhāṣya (after the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi): bibboka is disregard, out of pride and māna, even for what one desires; moṭṭāyita, the longing that wakes in the heart at the memory of the beloved or at talk of him; maugdhya, asking the beloved about what one knows as if one did not know; cakita, great fear before the beloved where there is nothing to fear.
  41. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: Kṛṣṇa says, “Until You pay the toll, I forbid You to go along this road,” and so begins the toll-collecting pastime (dāna-keli).
  42. Heading in the edition: “A comparison with a sweet drink.”
  43. Heading in the edition: “the words of Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī”. Anubhāṣya: all seven bhāvas are in this glance — the smile, weeping, anger (the reddened corners), pride and longing (brimming with playful delight) and fear (the narrowing).
  44. Heading in the edition: “a verse of the Gosvāmipāda”.
  45. Heading in the edition: “Speaking of Lakṣmī’s majesty, Śrīvāsa teases Svarūpa.”
  46. Anubhāṣya: the Lord’s “own servants” are Gadādhara and the others who form His potency (śakti); they are wholly devoted to the service of Śrī Rādhā-Govinda and absorbed in rāgātmikā-bhakti.
  47. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: Vṛndāvana-dhāma is the place where Kṛṣṇa, setting majesty aside, counts Himself rich in the sweetness of leaves, flowers and the like.
  48. Anubhāṣya (on 227): the supreme light there — the moon, the sun and the rest — is made of spiritual bliss and is meant to be relished.
  49. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: there dwell countless millions of Lakṣmīs full of sweetness, who have surpassed the Lakṣmī of majesty.
  50. Anubhāṣya: the goddesses of fortune are the gopīs; the Lover is the One without a second enjoyer; the trees yield the fruit of love for Kṛṣṇa; everything there is beyond matter and meant for Kṛṣṇa’s enjoyment alone.
  51. Heading in the edition: “the words of Bilvamaṅgala, quoted in the Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, Dakṣiṇa-vibhāga, first wave”.
  52. The edition prints nikaṭe āise without nā (“not”), an evident misprint: the edition’s headings (“Fearing to disturb the rasa, Nitāi praises the Lord from afar”; “As Nitāi does not come near…”) and the Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya confirm the reading “does not come near”. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: seeing that the Lord, in the rapture of Rādhā’s love, had shown the form of Rādhikā, Nityānanda Prabhu kept at a distance, for it did not befit his position (adhikāra-virodha).
  53. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: some doubt whether Lakṣmī-devī’s prasāda may be taken — yet Mahāprabhu Himself took it with His devotees. Lakṣmī and all the potencies are the Lord’s maidservants: they offer what is given to them to their Lord and only then partake, so the prasāda of His servants and maidservants is to be honoured as the prasāda of Bhagavān Himself.
  54. Heading in the edition: “During the pahāṇḍi the silk rope partly gives way.”
  55. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: silk is woven in many villages near Kulīna-grāma, and so the Lord charged Rāmānanda Vasu and Satyarāja Khān, as yajamānas, with bringing the silk ropes.
  56. Heading in the edition: “He shows the devotees the Herā-pañcamī and reveals the pastimes of Vraja.”
  57. The same colophon as Madhya 7.155; translation as there.
